description: Model profiles for Rihal Code agents (v1.0-beta). Each profile maps every agent to a specific model tier. Switch profiles at runtime to balance quality vs cost vs runtime compatibility.

quality.description: Maximum reasoning power. Opus for all decision-making and research agents, Sonnet for execution and review, Haiku for summary tasks. Use when: quota available, critical architecture work, strategic demos.

balanced.description: Smart allocation (default). Opus only for deep-reasoning agents — strategists, CTO, planning, research. Sonnet for execution and structured work. Haiku for high-volume summaries. Use when: normal day-to-day development.

budget.description: Minimum cost. Sonnet for reasoning agents, Haiku for everything else. Use when: pricing constraints, experiments, prototyping.

inherit.description: Follow the current session model. All agents resolve to 'inherit'. Best when you switch models interactively (e.g., OpenCode /model command) or when using non-Anthropic providers (OpenRouter, local models) — otherwise Rihal Code may call Anthropic models directly, incurring unexpected costs.

model_aliases.description: Short names for the common Claude models in 2026. These are used throughout the profiles table.

resolution_rules.description: How to resolve which model an agent should use at dispatch time
steps: 1. Read .rihal/config.json (project-level config). If `model_overrides.{agent}` is set, use that.
2. If no override, look up the agent in the current profile's `agents` map.
3. If the result is 'inherit', return null/empty to let the runtime pick.
4. If the result is a tier name (opus/sonnet/haiku), resolve via model_aliases.
5. If it's a fully-qualified model ID, pass it through unchanged.

per_project_config_example.description: Example .rihal/config.json for per-project model profile + overrides

runtime_compatibility.description: Different runtimes need different model ID formats
runtime_compatibility.claude_code: Use short aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku) or full Anthropic model IDs
runtime_compatibility.codex: Set profile to 'inherit' OR use model_overrides with OpenAI IDs (o3, o4-mini)
runtime_compatibility.opencode: Use 'inherit' profile to follow the live /model selection
runtime_compatibility.gemini_cli: Use 'inherit' profile and model_overrides with Gemini IDs (google/gemini-2.5-pro)
runtime_compatibility.openrouter: Use 'inherit' profile and model_overrides with OpenRouter IDs (anthropic/claude-opus-4-6)
runtime_compatibility.local: Use 'inherit' profile — runtime picks based on loaded model

design_rationale.why_opus_for_sadiq: Strategic framing affects months of work. Opus handles multi-variable optimization better.
design_rationale.why_opus_for_waleed: Architecture decisions have year-2 change cost. Opus reasons about trade-offs more reliably.
design_rationale.why_opus_for_hussain_pm: PRD scope decisions need careful trade-off reasoning across stakeholders.
design_rationale.why_opus_for_planner: Plan quality determines execution velocity; bad plans compound across the whole phase.
design_rationale.why_opus_for_architect: Architecture reviews flag long-term consequences that cheaper models miss.
design_rationale.why_sonnet_for_executors: Execution follows explicit plan instructions. Sonnet handles this reliably at lower cost.
design_rationale.why_sonnet_for_reviewers: Code review benefits from strong reasoning but doesn't require opus-level for structured outputs.
design_rationale.why_haiku_for_writers: Documentation and summary tasks are high-volume and structured — Haiku is fast and cheap.
design_rationale.why_inherit_profile: Some runtimes let users switch models at runtime. Inherit keeps all agents aligned to that live selection. Also required for non-Anthropic providers.
